cards.condition: Contiguous tensor axes and suspected excess memory transactions.
cards.evidence: Strides and measured traffic efficiency; timing alone cannot establish coalescing.
cards.transformation: Map neighboring lanes to neighboring addresses.
cards.tradeoff: Layout changes can increase address computation or hurt reuse.

cards.condition: Operands are reused across output tiles.
cards.evidence: Tile dimensions, bytes per output and compiler resource reports.
cards.transformation: Explore larger tiles to reuse loaded operands.
cards.tradeoff: Larger tiles consume more registers/shared memory and can reduce active blocks.

cards.condition: Input dtype and fixed tolerances support matrix instructions.
cards.evidence: Dtype, reference errors and instruction availability.
cards.transformation: Use tiled dot products with FP32 accumulation when valid.
cards.tradeoff: Numerical order changes and alignment/padding overhead require validation.

cards.evidence: Compiler registers, shared bytes and spills; occupancy counters if available.
cards.transformation: Compare tile sizes or warp counts while tracking latency.
cards.tradeoff: Occupancy is diagnostic; increasing it can sacrifice reuse or instruction efficiency.

cards.evidence: Launch count and lower-bound intermediate traffic.
cards.tradeoff: Live values increase register pressure; fusion may reduce parallelism.

cards.evidence: Rows, row width and resource use.
cards.transformation: Compare per-row parallel reductions with different warp counts.
cards.tradeoff: More warps add reduction communication; wide rows may spill.

cards.condition: Dimensions are not multiples of tiles.
cards.evidence: Shape remainder and failed boundary validation.
cards.transformation: Mask boundary loads/stores with reduction-appropriate neutral values.
cards.tradeoff: Padding can waste work, especially for short or irregular dimensions.

cards.evidence: Stall measurements if available and stage-count timing sweeps.
cards.transformation: Compare a small number of software-pipeline stage counts.
cards.tradeoff: Extra stages use shared memory and can lower residency.

cards.condition: Small workloads or many short kernels.
cards.evidence: Launch count and timing across size configurations.
cards.transformation: Reduce launches or increase useful work per program.
cards.tradeoff: Fewer programs can underutilize the GPU; timing alone is insufficient to diagnose host overhead.

cards.condition: Exponentials or normalization are sensitive to input scale.
cards.evidence: Extreme/constant inputs and fixed error tolerances.
cards.transformation: Use stable reductions, subtract row maxima for softmax, and preserve normalization epsilon.
cards.tradeoff: Additional stable arithmetic can cost instructions; correctness takes precedence.

cards.condition: Program count is small relative to SM count.
cards.evidence: Grid dimensions, SM count and measured latency.
cards.transformation: Reduce per-program tile size to expose independent work.
cards.tradeoff: Additional blocks duplicate loads and scheduling overhead.

cards.condition: An apparent speedup is close to timing variability.
cards.evidence: Paired latency samples and interquartile ranges.
cards.transformation: Remeasure candidate and incumbent nearby before retention.
cards.tradeoff: Extra measurement consumes GPU time; it avoids choosing noise.
